key_insight: Discrete diffusion models can have an ODE-based formulation analogous to the probability flow ODE used in continuous diffusion. The paper introduces exponential residual flows (ERFs), which pair discrete states with continuous residual variables.
problem_solved: Continuous diffusion has a deterministic ODE formulation that supports accelerated sampling and consistency distillation. This paper addresses whether an analogous formulation exists for discrete diffusion models.
method: Introduce exponential residual flows as an ODE-based framework for discrete diffusion.
Augment each discrete state with a continuous residual variable.
Use the augmented representation to establish a discrete-diffusion analogue of probability flow.
impact: This framework could provide a foundation for accelerated sampling and consistency distillation in discrete diffusion models. The supplied abstract is truncated, so specific algorithms, speedups, and experimental results cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: continuous diffusion with probability flow ODE versus discrete diffusion with ERFs.
Augmented-state diagram showing a discrete state paired with a continuous residual variable.
Trajectory illustration contrasting continuous residual evolution with changes in discrete state.
Conceptual pipeline: discrete diffusion → ERF formulation → potential sampling and distillation applications.
paper_title: An ODE-based Sampler for Discrete Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Samson Gourevitch, Yazid Janati, Eric Moulines, Eric P. Xing, Alain Durmus
